"This was good." They mean it.
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."

lines: d28: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Jada Zaitsev is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d28: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d28: 🕯️ Jada is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d28: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d28: 🕯️ Jada Zaitsev is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d28: What Jada kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d28: "Jada's gone." Esmeralda looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Jada." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d28: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Hank blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d28: 📖 LEARNED: Intimidating Presence (Level 1). You don't have to fight. Most people decide not to, just looking at you.

d28: 📖 LEARNED: Bodyguard (Level 1). In the wilds, when a blow is falling on someone beside you, you step into it. Once per fight, an attack meant for your ally lands on you instead. It hurts. That's the job.
d28: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d28: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d28: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Jada Zaitsev, 28 days. The mantle passes to Hank Dixon.
d28: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Hank Dixon, 48 — a night security guard. His hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Echo Location.
d28: The village's quarrel was with Jada — and Jada is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d28: At the grave, Zoey, Esmeralda, Ingrid and 2 more speak for Hank — "Jada trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d28: The fire knew Hank before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
